title: AWS EC2 and VPC Networking: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of EC2 instance types, pricing models and AMIs, plus VPC networking: regions and AZs, subnets, route tables, internet and NAT gateways, and security groups vs NACLs.

chapters.title: What This Handbook Covers
points: Regions and AZs
VPC and CIDR
Subnets and route tables
IGW and NAT gateway
Security groups vs NACLs
EC2 types, AMIs, pricing

chapters.title: Regions, AZs and the VPC Mental Model
points: A Region is an isolated geographic area with 3+ AZs; an AZ is one or more data centres. Most resources are regional or AZ-scoped, and IAM is global.
A VPC is your private network inside one Region and spans all its AZs. Pick a primary CIDR between /16 and /28, such as 10.0.0.0/16, and keep it clear of other VPCs and on-prem ranges.
A VPC is regional while a subnet lives in exactly one AZ. For high availability, put one subnet per AZ in at least 2 AZs.
Mistake: overlapping CIDRs block VPC peering and VPN, and the primary CIDR cannot be changed later. Mistake: using the default VPC for production.
Interview Point: Is a subnet regional or zonal? How do you make an app survive an AZ failure? Why do CIDR choices matter for peering?

chapters.title: Subnets, Route Tables, IGW and NAT
points: A subnet is public only if its route table has 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to an Internet Gateway (IGW). A private subnet has no IGW route. The 'public' label comes from the route, not the subnet.
Every subnet has one route table, and the most specific (longest-prefix) route wins. The local route for the VPC CIDR is always present and cannot be removed.

An IGW is free, horizontally scaled, and lets instances reach the internet only if they also have a public or Elastic IP. A zonal NAT gateway sits in a public subnet with an Elastic IP (a regional NAT gateway needs no public subnet and spans AZs automatically) and gives private subnets outbound-only internet via 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-id.

Example: public subnet route 0.0.0.0/0 -> igw-xxx. Private subnet route 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-xxx. For HA with zonal NAT gateways, deploy one per AZ (a regional NAT gateway spans AZs itself). NAT gateways are billed hourly plus per GB of data processed.

Mistake: a NAT gateway placed in a private subnet, or an instance with no public IP in a public subnet, still cannot reach the internet. Interview Point: What makes a subnet public? NAT gateway vs IGW? Why one NAT gateway per AZ?

chapters.title: Security Groups vs NACLs
points: A security group (SG) is attached to an ENI/instance and is stateful: return traffic is automatically allowed. It supports allow rules only, and the default is deny inbound and allow all outbound.

A NACL is attached to a subnet and is stateless: you must allow return traffic yourself, including ephemeral ports 1024-65535. It has numbered allow and deny rules evaluated lowest first, with the first match winning and an implicit deny at the end.

Comparison: SG is instance-level, stateful, allow-only, and evaluates all rules. NACL is subnet-level, stateless, allow and deny, and evaluates rules in order. Use a NACL to block a specific IP, since an SG cannot deny.

Example: the web SG allows 443 from 0.0.0.0/0, and the DB SG allows 5432 from source = web-SG id (reference an SG, not an IP). Mistake: a custom NACL that omits the ephemeral outbound range breaks replies.
Interview Point: Stateful vs stateless? How do you block one malicious IP? Can an SG reference another SG? Why can a connection fail even when the SG is open?

chapters.title: EC2 Instance Types, AMIs and Pricing Models
points: Instance family letters: T/M general purpose, C compute, R/X memory, I/D storage, P/G GPU. Names read family+generation+size, e.g. m7g.large, where g means Graviton/Arm. T-types are burstable and use CPU credits.

An AMI is a regional template (root volume snapshot, launch permissions, block device mapping) used to launch instances. Copy it to another Region to use it there, and share it by account ID. Instance store data is lost on stop, while EBS persists.

Pricing: On-Demand is pay per second with no commitment. Reserved/Savings Plans give up to ~72% off for a 1 or 3 year commitment. Spot gives up to ~90% off but AWS can reclaim it with a 2-minute warning, so it suits fault-tolerant work. Dedicated Hosts are for licensing and compliance.

Example: a steady baseline on a Savings Plan, spiky load on On-Demand, and batch or CI jobs on Spot. Launch with a security group, key pair, subnet, and an IAM instance profile for AWS access instead of access keys.

Mistake: leaving stopped instances with EBS volumes or unattached Elastic IPs running up cost, or using Spot for stateful databases. Interview Point: Spot vs Reserved? What is an AMI and is it regional? Why choose a T instance, and what happens when credits run out?

chapters.title: AWS EC2 and VPC Cheat Sheet
points: Public subnet = route 0.0.0.0/0 -> IGW; private subnet outbound = 0.0.0.0/0 -> zonal NAT gateway placed in a public subnet (a regional NAT gateway needs no public subnet).
Scope: VPC is regional, subnet is one AZ, SG is instance-level, NACL is subnet-level, AMI is regional.
SG: stateful, allow only. NACL: stateless, allow and deny, ordered rules, ephemeral ports 1024-65535 for return traffic.
Pricing: On-Demand = flexible, Savings Plan/Reserved = steady load, Spot = interruptible (2-minute notice), Dedicated Host = licence or compliance.

Checklist: use non-overlapping CIDRs, 2+ AZs, one zonal NAT gateway per AZ (or one regional NAT gateway), SG-to-SG references, IAM roles rather than keys, and an IGW route plus public IP before expecting internet access.
Interview Point: Walk a request from the internet to a private DB: IGW, route table, NACL, SG, instance. Where could it be blocked at each step?
